children: gained in early action on Wednesday after Jefferies upgraded the restaurant stock to a Buy rating after having it set at Hold. The firm sees an attractive entry point following the pullback in the share price and relative underperformance to casual dining peers. The stock slide is considered overdone for a consistent, quality growth story that is expected to continue to see above-peer sales and EBITDA growth.

"We expect the casual dining category's same-store sales to remain resilient, and note recent trends have outperformed that of the broader industry, which we believe can be attributed to shifting preferences towards more experiential dining-out occasions that consumers continue to budget for," highlighted analyst Andy Barish. Another positive factor for Texas Roadhouse
is easing beef inflation that could boost the company's COGS margin rate, according to Barish.
Jefferies assigned a price target of $190 to Texas Roadhouse
, which works out to a 14X multiple to the firm's 2027 EBITDA estimate.
broke 2.5% higher in premarket trading to $166.20 vs. the 52-week range of $153.83 to $216.30. Wall Street analysts and Seeking Alpha analysts both have a consensus Buy rating on the restaurant name.
